merger_name: Herron Todd White Group - Mitchell Brandtman

anzsic_codes.name: Engineering Design and Engineering Consulting Services

merger_description:
Herron Todd White (One) Pty Ltd (**HTW One**) proposes to acquire 100% of the shares in Mitchell Brandtman Pty Ltd (**Mitchell Brandtman**) (the **Acquisition**).

As part of the Acquisition, shareholders of Mitchell Brandtman will be issued shares in the ultimate parent company of HTW One – Herron Todd White (Holdings) Pty Ltd (**HTW Holdings**). Post-completion, those shareholders will collectively own 7.4% of the shares in HTW Holdings.

HTW Holdings and its direct and indirect subsidiaries (collectively, **HTW**) provide property valuation and related property advisory services throughout Australia. HTW’s core service offering comprises residential, commercial and agribusiness property valuation services, supplied principally to Australian authorised deposit-taking institutions such as the major banks and other financial institutions, as well as to government agencies, property developers, legal practitioners and private clients. HTW is majority-owned by funds managed by QPE No. 7 Management Pty Ltd, an entity within the Quadrant Private Equity (**QPE**) group.

Mitchell Brandtman provides quantity surveying and related services for construction purposes – including construction cost planning, construction financier quantity surveying, infrastructure cost, and related construction cost advisory services – primarily to developers, financiers, contractors, lawyers, property investors, architects and government bodies. Mitchell Brandtman operates from offices in Brisbane, the Gold Coast, Sydney, Miranda, Canberra, and Melbourne.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given:
a. there is no horizontal overlap or vertical relationship
between HTW and Mitchell Brandtman in Australia
• b. there are alternative suppliers of both property valuation and
advisory services and quantity surveying services in
Australia
c. there is a low risk of foreclosure or other concerning
conglomerate effects resulting from exclusionary conduct,
bundling or tying of products and services post-acquisition.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
